Streaming snapshots merge by field maximum, abandoned branches count, store-reported totals settle cache relations, and ambiguous fields stay visible notes. Sidecar fingerprints cover JCode journals, Fx session metadata, editor conversation histories, Command Code config and ZCode/Unsloth WAL files.

All 54 Pulse 1.9 Token sources registered with a reader each: Grok Build, Devin, Devin Desktop, CodeBuddy, WorkBuddy, Antigravity CLI, Antigravity IDE, Trae, Warp, Copilot, OmO Native, Prime Agent and Freebuff added on top of the 41 already present; Warp and Freebuff report no token counts by the original design and say so instead of estimating

Window starter: per-provider opt-in with a risk confirmation, shared local hours, reset-plus-grace scheduling, first-account-only rule, one attempt per reset, recorded outcome, and a settings group on the Claude Code and Codex panes

User extensions: manifest scan with schema/id/executable-path validation, off by default, per-extension switch, 1-60 s timeout, output ceiling and JSON validation, failure classification, one account per extension in the panel, a User extensions settings pane and a per-extension account group

Official service status rewritten as a 45-entry catalogue (44 providers plus the second MiniMax storefront) over 12 feed shapes with the original's five-rule component matching, 7 palettes, per-feed single-request outage checks and OutageMemory keyed by provider id

Currency conversion for the original's 7 display currencies: estimates only (a service's own balance, credits and console charges keep the currency the service stated), network only when the chosen currency is not USD, manual rate overrides
Token spend spans widened from 3 to the original's 9 including a custom start/end day pair; a one-day range swaps the day bars for the hour profile as the original does
Extension metrics rendered with hand-written SVG trends on the card (at most two, like the original's metricTrendLimit) and in Settings (every series), with no new dependency

Hide from screen capture via Tauri's set_content_protected, which tao maps to SetWindowDisplayAffinity(hwnd, WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE) on Windows and the original's NSWindow.sharingType on macOS; off by default, and a request rather than a guarantee

Model-price spellings follow ModelPrices.swift: `-extra-low` effort, Gemini `-n`/`-control`/`-xpe` tags, `-[0-9]+[kKmM]` context windows and Kimi's `k3`/`k2p6` abbreviations resolve to the base model; `grok-build-0.1` stays distinct and only one tag is stripped
Settings test-notification button sends the same Windows notification path as quota and recap alerts and reports success or the permission failure
Proxy mode 不使用代理 (the original's direct mode) connects without any proxy even when the environment or Windows configures one, hands no proxy key to CLI children and keeps the updater's own policy

Kimi Code's ~/.kimi-code session store is read next to the legacy ~/.kimi wire logs: usage.record counters, provider-prefixed model names stripped and priced through the Kimi aliases, and a migrated request folds by second plus counters instead of counting twice

Recaps offer 日报/周报 beside 月报/年报: day and week keys follow RecapPeriods.swift (a week starts on the reader's first weekday), day/week cards drop the calendar, a finished day compares with the day before while a running day has no chip, payback is prorated per day across the months the week touches, the week opener gives each tool a seven-day strip, and the week scorecard shows seven daily pips

Progress-bar styles follow UsageBar.swift: continuous (6 px) or segmented (12 px ticks with a 2.5 px tick, 2 px gap and whole-tick lighting), selectable in Appearance and shared by the card and tray menu

Qoder credit parts follow QoderUsageService.swift: plan, resource-pack and dedicated rows with their own expiry when showsParts is enabled, a de-duplicated total expiry, and a 31-day credit history with today/7-day/31-day used and charged totals plus a daily bar chart

Cursor weekly-limit plans show the weekly 7d ring and reset instead of the two monthly pools; enterprise accounts show one monthly USD allowance and on-demand spend keeps its own row, with the legacy usage endpoint retained as a fallback
Codex weaker-model signals follow 1.12.4: max and ultra effort ranks participate in comparisons while the Codex context-window setting is no longer treated as a server-side downgrade
The Settings window follows the system-settings layout: a sticky title bar names the page, back/forward history buttons cover pane moves and Alt+Left/Right shortcuts work from anywhere in the window

Experimental liquid docking is off by default: pulling a docked rail away eases it behind the pointer, thins and scales the panel, and releases it past an 80 pt break distance; the notch capsule waits 250 ms of stillness before expanding
Connection diagnostics in each account pane show the latest check result, its time, the displayed source and a credential-free copyable summary of the reported windows

Developer integrations: a settings pane documents the read-only --json/--statusline/--recap output, copies commands, saves a PowerShell status-line script or exports a PowerShell/POSIX developer kit, and shows pulsewin://account links (including extra accounts) plus a pulsewin://recap shortcut that opens the Token Spend recap; the NSIS installer registers the pulsewin:// URL protocol, and the app accepts only the settings/account/recap navigation paths (a URL cannot change settings, run commands or start a login)
The --recap command prints one day, week, month or year of real Token figures as read-only JSON, refuses when Token Spend reading is off, and writes no setting

Model spend detail shows the selected model's daily input, cache write, cache read, output and total columns in a table that sorts by any column and pages in tens, measured output speed and first-token latency from reply timing, and estimated cache-read savings on the Token split
The Token split's cache-read figure has a hover/focus card showing cached tokens, its share of the input side, cache-write tokens and the estimated cache-read savings

DeepSeek console renewal: a saved login that the console has signed out is renewed from Chrome, Edge, Brave or Chromium LevelDB stores after the token is verified against the account summary, and Settings can import the browser session explicitly.
OpenCode console renewal: a signed-out read re-reads the app WebView cookie jar for opencode.ai console sessions, saves the renewed sign-in and retries the workspace read once.

DeepSeek and OpenCode Go console ledgers feed their detailed cards: one record per console day with the day's tokens, its top model and the console-reported cost, so the card's 31-day figures, chart, speed and cache summaries use the service's own accounting instead of local transcripts.

The monthly recap reminder's Windows toast opens the Token Spend recap when activated: the notification is sent through notify-rust and its WinRT activation callback routes a body click to the recap view, because the Tauri notification plugin exposes no desktop action events
